messages:
lara-sec: NOVAMED kicked back our security questionnaire. asks: an example Okta->Redwood mapping for PD and Dev teams, a signed / tamper-evident audit export for the past 90 days, options for customer-managed keys (HSM vs Azure/AWS KMS), and a reproducible incident replay runbook for their security team. also asked about FIPS mode and attestation.

sam-infra: got it. we should show three key patterns: 1) customer HSM where keys never leave customer HSM (PKCS#11 / CloudHSM import), 2) envelope keys wrapped by customer KMS (AWS/GCP/Azure) with us holding only wrapped key, 3) service-managed keys with audit signatures from our service key. include a diagram.

lara-sec: NOVAMED wants a firm statement about importing keys into our hosted HSM vs private deployments. what DO we support?

mike-crypto: short answer: hosted-> we do NOT allow customers to import raw keys into our hosted HSM. hosted customers can enable Customer-Managed KMS wrapping (CMK) where data keys are encrypted by their KMS. private deployments (on-prem or VPC) can integrate with customer HSMs or allow keys to be provisioned into the local HSM under customer control. add note about Azure Key Vault and BYOK flow too.

ops-bot: reminder: compliance checklist item 7.2 requires attestation statement for HSM imports.

lara-sec: good. include an attest template. also NOVAMED asked for the exact audit export steps and how we prove integrity. can we show commands and checksums?

sam-infra: yes. sample flow: export -> compute sha256 -> create detached signature with tenant envelope key -> upload to S3 with manifest -> emit audit event. example commands below.

sam-infra: ```bash
# export tenant logs (ndjson)
rictl audit export --tenant novamed --from 2025-11-01 --to 2026-02-28 --format ndjson --out novamed-20251101-20260228.ndjson
# compute checksum
sha256sum novamed-20251101-20260228.ndjson > novamed.sha256
# sign (detached) with envelope key
rictl crypto sign --key /opt/keys/tenant_envelope.pem --in novamed-20251101-20260228.ndjson --out novamed.sig --detached
# bundle and upload
tar czf novamed-audit-bundle.tgz novamed-20251101-20260228.ndjson novamed.sha256 novamed.sig manifest.json
aws s3 cp novamed-audit-bundle.tgz s3://redwood-sec/exports/novamed/ --server-side-encryption aws:kms
```

mike-crypto: include how to verify: provide public cert + detached signature verification steps. also include an option to have the bundle signed by the customer's HSM if they prefer (private deployment). mention we publish our verification certificate fingerprint in the attestation.

lara-sec: great. next: incident replay/runbook. NOVAMED wants to be able to reproduce a sequence from logs in a sandbox without touching production resources. keep it tight.

tess-sre: propose this minimal replay runbook: 1) create ephemeral replay tenant with network egress blocked, 2) import signed audit bundle, 3) run `rictl audit replay --input novamed.ndjson --replay-tenant replay-novamed --sandbox --block-external` with a dry-run first, 4) run specific scenario IDs, 5) collect debug traces and sign results. sample: 

```bash
# create sandbox tenant
rictl tenant create --name replay-novamed --tags replay,sandbox --no-egress
# import
rictl audit import --tenant replay-novamed --in novamed-20251101-20260228.ndjson --signed novamed.sig --verify-cert /certs/redwood_pub.pem
# replay a specific session
rictl audit replay --tenant replay-novamed --session 2026-01-15T13:22:11Z --sandbox --block-external --trace out/trace-20260115.json
```

tess-sre: include guardrails: RBAC (only audit-read/replay roles), network ACLs (default deny egress), quota limits, and a mandatory review step before enabling any outbound connectors.

lara-sec: perfect. last piece: vuln triage / SLA. NOVAMED asked how we handle infra deps and CVEs. keep it short.

mike-crypto: we maintain a dependency inventory and run routine scans. SLA: critical exploitability assessments within 24 hours of disclosure; mitigations (patch or workaround / rollback) within 72 hours, unless blocking business constraints—then we provide compensating controls and a schedule. include a small example: OpenSSL CVE-2025-9999 -> triaged, emergency patch applied in 48h, canary rolled, and full rollout in 7 days.

lara-sec: add retention & evidence: we keep raw audit lines 90 days by default, aggregated/indices 365 days, configurable for Dedicated. provide legal attestation template and SOC2 link. add FIPS/HSM note: for FIPS mode we run validated crypto modules in private deployments and provide HSM attestation reports on request.

sam-infra: i'll draw the keyflow diagram for three patterns (customer-hsm, customer-kms-wrap, service-managed) and drop it in the draft.

lara-sec: action items: sam -> keyflow diagram + export commands; tess -> replay runbook + guardrails; mike -> attestation template + CVE example wording. i'll assemble the reply to NOVAMED and propose a call next Wed. tagging @ops-bot to create the export bucket and thumbprint. :white_check_mark:

ops-bot: export-bucket created: s3://redwood-sec/exports/3471230000-novamed/  cert-thumbprint: SHA256:4b:9c:2d:... stored at s3://redwood-sec/exports/3471230000-novamed/thumbprint.txt

tess-sre: thanks - i'll start the replay template and leave a checklist for the security reviewer.

lara-sec: thanks everyone. i'll post the draft here for review by EOD tomorrow.
